title: Relative Hom functions extend independently of fully faithful witnesses
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal P,\mathcal Q$ be categories [def-nagata-category], let $C:\mathcal A\to\mathcal P$ induce bijections on all Hom sets, and let $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal Q$ be a full subcategory. Give functors $F,E:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$, $J,G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal P$, a natural isomorphism $q:F\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ and natural bijections
$$a_{K,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal Q}(FK,Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(K,JY),\qquad b_{L,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal Q}(ECL,Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(CL,GY),$$
for $K\in\mathcal P$, $L\in\mathcal A$, $Y\in\mathcal D$, with naturality in both variables as in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Suppose a natural isomorphism $\theta:J\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ satisfies
$$b_{L,Y}(h q_{CL}^{-1})=\theta_Ya_{CL,Y}(h)$$
for every $h:FCL\to Y$. If $\alpha:CL\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ is an isomorphism, define for $z:EK\to Y$
$$b^\alpha_{K,Y}(z)=b_{L,Y}(z E(\alpha))\alpha^{-1}.$$
Then this is a bijection and
$$b^\alpha_{K,Y}(h q_K^{-1})=\theta_Ya_{K,Y}(h)$$
for every $h:FK\to Y$. For any second witness $\beta:CL'\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ there is a unique isomorphism $t:L\xrightarrow{\sim}L'$ with $C(t)=\beta^{-1}\alpha$, and $b^\alpha_{K,Y}=b^\beta_{K,Y}$. Thus $b^\alpha$ defines a natural family $\bar b$ on the full subcategory of objects isomorphic to some $CL$, independent of the witness. Its inverse satisfies
$$\bar b_{K,Y}^{-1}(\theta_Y g)=a_{K,Y}^{-1}(g)q_K^{-1}.$$
Any already specified natural relative Hom bijection whose value at the identity witness is $b$ is equal to $\bar b$. In particular, the units and counits obtained from these Hom functions by transposing identities [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] agree under $q,\theta$ whenever they are defined: if $FK\in\mathcal D$, then $\bar b_{K,FK}(q_K^{-1})=\theta_{FK}a_{K,FK}(1_{FK})$; if $JY$ lies in the stated full subcategory, then
$$\bar b_{JY,Y}(a_{JY,Y}^{-1}(1_{JY})q_{JY}^{-1})=\theta_Y.$$
These assertions impose no relative adjunction outside the stated domains. Composition is read right to left.

proof.text: For every K in P and Y in D, construct e(K,Y) as the composite of the Hom equivalence given by precomposition with q_K, a(K,Y), and postcomposition with theta_Y. These are Mathlib Iso.homFromEquiv and Iso.homToEquiv, so the composite is an equivalence with value a(K,Y)(q_K followed by z) followed by theta_Y. After Step 2 identifies the transported witness function with e(K,Y), its bijectivity follows from Equiv.bijective.

proof.text:
Naturality of $q$ gives $q_K^{-1}E(\alpha)=F(\alpha)q_{CL}^{-1}$. Thus the assumed equality on $CL$ and naturality of $a$ give
$$b^\alpha_{K,Y}(hq_K^{-1})=b_{L,Y}(hF(\alpha)q_{CL}^{-1})\alpha^{-1}=\theta_Ya_{CL,Y}(hF(\alpha))\alpha^{-1}=\theta_Ya_{K,Y}(h).$$
Taking $h=zq_K$ yields $b^\alpha_{K,Y}(z)=\theta_Ya_{K,Y}(zq_K)$.

proof.text: The bijective Hom maps give a FullyFaithful structure via Mathlib Functor.FullyFaithful.nonempty_iff_map_bijective. Its isoEquiv is an equivalence between isomorphisms L to L-prime and isomorphisms CL to CL-prime, with forward map C.mapIso. Apply its inverse to alpha followed by beta inverse. The right inverse law proves the specified image, and injectivity gives uniqueness.

proof.text: The last formula in Step 2 contains no witness, so both witness functions equal the equivalence e(K,Y) constructed in Step 1. Define bar(K,Y)=e(K,Y) for K in the essential image. For f:K-prime to K, naturality of q moves q_K-prime past E(f), and naturality of a gives bar(K-prime,Y)(E(f) followed by z)=f followed by bar(K,Y)(z). For v:Y to Y-prime, naturality of a followed by naturality of theta gives bar(K,Y-prime)(z followed by v)=bar(K,Y)(z) followed by G(v).

proof.text: Substitute $h=a_{K,Y}^{-1}(g)$ in Step 2. It gives $\bar b_{K,Y}(a_{K,Y}^{-1}(g)q_K^{-1})=\theta_Yg$. Bijectivity from Step 1 proves exactly the asserted inverse formula.

proof.text: Let $d$ be any already specified natural family on the same full subcategory with $d_{CL,Y}=b_{L,Y}$ at the identity witness. Naturality at $\alpha:CL\to K$ gives $d_{K,Y}(z)\alpha=b_{L,Y}(zE(\alpha))$. Composing with $\alpha^{-1}$ proves $d_{K,Y}(z)=b^\alpha_{K,Y}(z)=\bar b_{K,Y}(z)$.

proof.text: For K in the essential image with FK in D, apply the normalization formula of Step 2 to the identity of FK, canceling composition with the identity, to obtain the stated unit comparison. For Y in D with JY in the essential image, apply that formula to a(JY,Y).symm(identity). The inverse law of the equivalence a and the category identity law give theta_Y, which is precisely the stated counit comparison. These are substitutions in relative Hom functions and do not construct a global adjunction.
